skill.name: figjam-plugin
skill.description: FigJam plugin development workflow. Use when modifying code.ts (canvas rendering), ui.ts (WebSocket/UI), fixing plugin build errors, or adding new rendering features.
skill.summary: Guides FigJam plugin changes across canvas rendering, UI messaging, builds, and local Figma import.
skill.author: 7nohe

content.value_statement: FigJam plugin changes can fail when main-thread and UI APIs are mixed. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through the project structure, build flow, and import workflow.
actual_capabilities: Explains the split between code.ts and ui.ts responsibilities.
Identifies which APIs belong in the plugin main thread.
Shows the local build command for the plugin package.
Describes how to import the manifest in Figma Desktop.
Documents debugging locations for UI and main-thread errors.
Summarizes JSON import handling and validation behavior.
limitations: It does not include source code for the plugin implementation.
It does not validate manifest contents by itself.
It assumes the project uses the documented packages/plugin layout.
It does not replace Figma Desktop testing.

use_cases.title: Add Canvas Rendering
use_cases.description: Use the skill to place rendering changes in code.ts and keep browser APIs out of the main thread.

use_cases.title: Repair UI Messaging
use_cases.description: Use the skill to trace WebSocket, postMessage, and canvas communication when plugin data does not arrive.

use_cases.title: Prepare Local Plugin Testing
use_cases.description: Use the skill to build the package and import the manifest through Figma Desktop development tools.

prompt_templates.title: Locate the Right File
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to change a FigJam plugin feature. Tell me whether the change belongs in code.ts or ui.ts, and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Build Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this FigJam plugin build error. Identify the likely thread boundary issue and suggest the smallest fix.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Message Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace the CLI to UI to main-thread message flow for this plugin bug. List the checks I should run in order.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Rendering Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an implementation plan for a new FigJam rendering feature. Separate UI work, message passing, validation, and canvas rendering.

output_examples.input: I need to add a shape rendering feature to the plugin.
output_examples.output: The response separates canvas rendering work into code.ts, UI state into ui.ts, and validation checks before drawing.

output_examples.input: The plugin build succeeds, but Figma does not show the latest behavior.
output_examples.output: The response recommends rebuilding the plugin package, confirming the imported manifest path, and checking the correct Figma development console.

output_examples.input: A WebSocket message reaches the UI but nothing appears on the canvas.
output_examples.output: The response traces the UI postMessage handoff, main-thread handler, IR validation, and final figma API rendering step.

best_practices: Keep browser APIs in ui.ts and FigJam canvas APIs in code.ts.
Run the documented build before importing the manifest in Figma Desktop.
Check UI and main-thread consoles separately when debugging.
anti_patterns: Do not call window, document, fetch, or WebSocket from code.ts.
Do not treat WebSocket delivery as proof that canvas rendering succeeded.
Do not import a stale manifest after changing plugin package files.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents work on a FigJam plugin by following the documented file roles, build step, and debugging flow.

faq.question: Does it generate a full plugin?
faq.answer: No. It guides edits inside an existing plugin project with the documented packages/plugin structure.

faq.question: Which file handles canvas rendering?
faq.answer: The skill states that code.ts handles canvas rendering through figma APIs.

faq.question: Which file handles WebSocket UI work?
faq.answer: The skill states that ui.ts handles browser APIs, WebSocket behavior, and connection UI.

faq.question: How should I test changes locally?
faq.answer: Build the plugin package, then import packages/plugin/manifest.json through Figma Desktop development tools.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
